summary: DLMF 26.3 Lattice Paths: Binomial Coefficients: \genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m}{n} is the number of ways of choosing n objects from a collection of m distinct objects…
body: NIST DLMF section 26.3 (Lattice Paths: Binomial Coefficients) says: "\genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m}{n} is the number of ways of choosing n objects from a collection of m distinct objects without regard to order. \genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m+n}{n} is the number of lattice paths from (0,0) to (m,n) . See also 1.2(i) . The number of lattice paths from (0,0) to (m,n) , m\leq n , that stay on or above the line y=x is \genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m+n}{m}-\genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m+n}{m-1}. For numerical values of \genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m}{n} and \genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m+n}{n} see Tables 26.3.1 and 26.3.2 ." Equation 26.3.1 on the page has alt text "\genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m}{n}=\genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m}{m-n}=\frac{m!}{(m-n)!% \,n!},". Equation 26.3.2 on the page has alt text "\genfrac{(}{)}{0.0pt}{}{m}{n}=0,". This card records that section's wording and equation alt text. It does not retypeset a formula the alt text did not carry.
